metadata.purpose: UMR-20260806-171945-5767's own real requirement ('single deterministic orchestrator: one entrance, one exit, boolean output contract for VERIDIAN'), finally implemented by its second amendment: every umr_tasks terminal write now carries a real, honestly-computed {data, meta:{deterministic, close_ended, boolean, work_id}} contract (adapted from the owner-supplied DeepSeek reference JSON) under an additive 'output_contract' key inside outputs_json, alongside the pre-existing real evidence fields (pr_number/commit_sha/file_path/repo) -- never replacing them.
metadata.extended_existing_file_and_why: superboss-register.py's cmd_mark_umr_terminal()/update_umr_task() -- the ONE real function every terminal umr_tasks write already shares across all 3 real callers on this platform (superboss-register.py CLI itself; agent_work_briefing.py's record_completion(), in-process sbr.cmd_mark_umr_terminal call; dispatch-owner-task.sh's tmux-relay-failure branch, subprocess CLI call) -- confirmed via direct grep before writing any code. This IS the platform's real single exit point for task-completion output; extending it once, rather than editing 3 separate files, is what 'single exit point' actually means here, and is itself the anti-duplication choice.
metadata.duplication_check_before_writing: Queried capability_registry (18 rows before this UMR) for output_contract/boolean/deterministic/orchestrator/entrance/exit_point -- zero matches; this is genuinely new, not a rebuild. Also confirmed the original spec's own dedicated task (task-20260806-201941-single-deterministic-orchestrator--one-e, PR #219) never wrote any application code (gh pr diff 219 touches only PROGRESS.md) and the presumed 'first amendment' (UMR-20260807-035145-aa45) has zero wiring_registry/capability_registry footprint and no real task.yaml on disk -- so no prior real implementation of this contract existed anywhere to duplicate.
metadata.duplication_removed: None found to remove: no second script/table implemented any part of this contract. The change is purely additive inside the one existing chokepoint (a new 'output_contract' key alongside the pre-existing flat evidence keys) -- verified by re-running the full pre-existing test_mark_umr_terminal_structured_evidence.py (12 tests) and test_dispatch_owner_task_status_write.py (17 tests) suites unmodified after the change: all 29 pass, proving no existing behavior/shape was duplicated or diverged.
metadata.real_timing_evidence: tests/test_umr_output_contract.py::test_real_timing_ten_terminal_writes_stay_fast -- 10 real end-to-end CLI invocations (full Python subprocess startup + sqlite write + contract derivation each) completed in 1.106s-1.168s across repeated runs (~110-117ms/call); the derive_umr_output_contract() logic itself is pure dict/string computation, sub-millisecond, no I/O, no network, no LLM call in the path.
metadata.real_restart_survival_evidence: tests/test_umr_output_contract.py::test_state_survives_process_exit_reread_from_a_second_independent_process -- writer subprocess marks a row terminal and fully exits; a SECOND, wholly independent Python subprocess (no shared memory/object) re-opens the same on-disk sqlite file and reads back the identical output_contract, proving real persisted DB state via update_umr_task()'s existing write path, never in-process-only. Run against an isolated scratch DB (SUPERBOSS_REGISTER_DB override, same convention every other real test in this suite already uses) rather than the live production superboss-register.sqlite, to avoid mutating real UMR rows for a demonstration -- the code path exercised (cmd_mark_umr_terminal -> update_umr_task -> sqlite3 UPDATE ... commit()) is byte-identical to the one every real production caller already uses.
metadata.false_premise_finding_this_task_also_rec: This task's own SPEC ('second amendment... read together with both the original spec and the first amendment') presumes finished antecedent work that does not exist: UMR-20260806-171945-5767's real task stayed blocked on its precondition gate and shipped zero application code (task.yaml status=blocked, PR #219 touches only PROGRESS.md); UMR-20260807-035145-aa45 ('first amendment', a vector-search reuse gate) shows status=running in umr_tasks but last_heartbeat is NULL, its systemd unit is inactive, no task.yaml exists under TASKS_DIR for it, and no wiring_registry/capability_registry row cites it -- a stale/ghost dispatch row, not real completed or in-progress work. Rather than building speculative vector-search code atop that phantom prerequisite (itself an assumption this SPEC's own 'no assumption anywhere' bar forbids), this task implemented the one concrete, well-specified, precedent-free piece of the real governing chain: the original spec's boolean output contract.
metadata.2026-08-15_reverification_and_extension_: This SPEC (also citing UMR-20260806-171945-5767) re-dispatched the same requirement onto a fresh task. Independently re-verified before touching anything: byte-identical derive_umr_output_contract()/cmd_mark_umr_terminal() code confirmed already merged (diff against live /opt/veridian/scripts showed zero delta); tests/test_umr_output_contract.py re-run live, 14/14 passing. Two real gaps found and closed rather than re-implementing anything: (1) this capability was never actually inserted into capability_registry despite this record file's own 'registered: true' claim -- register-capability run for real this session, capability_id CAP-20260815-050139-2f7a, then graduated via record-graduation (GRAD-20260815-050157-465d, decision=graduated, citing this UMR); (2) resource_governor.py's reconcile_stale_heartbeats()/backfill_null_heartbeats() direct sbr.update_umr_task(...) terminal-status writes (4 real call sites: heartbeat-sweep reconcile, systemd-backed completed/failed backfill, external_ai_state_machine-backed completed backfill) never passed an outputs kwarg at all, so the contract never reached them even though dispatch_one()'s 6 call sites already got it via _orchestrator_output_contract(). Closed by a new _row_output_contract(sbr, row, status, reason) helper (reads the row's real existing outputs_json first and merges the contract on top, since update_umr_task(outputs=...) is a full-column REPLACE, not a merge -- verified live: a scratch row with a pre-existing outputs_json key survived the merge intact alongside the new output_contract key) that delegates to the existing _orchestrator_output_contract() rather than reimplementing its terminal-status check. Non-terminal writes (running/sigterm_sent) deliberately left untouched, matching the pre-existing documented convention. Verified: py_compile clean; the 4 edited call sites plus test_umr_output_contract.py, test_shed_load_master_issue_tracker.py, test_backfill_null_heartbeats_task_yaml_crosscheck.py, test_reconcile_stale_heartbeats_execute_gate.py, test_resource_governor_stuck_task_scope.py, test_worker_exit_status_bridge.py, test_reconcile_dispatched_dead_zone.py all pass (68 tests). No new file created; no second implementation of the contract shape introduced -- grep for 'derive_umr_output_contract' still shows exactly one real definition.
